title: Mozilla Otari Hackathon - Developers Wilding Jam Sesh #1!
description:
Hey! Marcus from Mozilla.org here! Thanks for your interest in the jam!

⭐️ Before you start, please star the Otari repo, it helps: [https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari](https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari) ⭐️

💬 Then join the Mozilla OSAI Discord through this link: [https://discord.gg/TqvzGH9mwz](https://discord.gg/TqvzGH9mwz). It gives you the `devs-wilding` role, which is how we reach entrants with updates, answers and results. 💬

# Welcome to Mozilla Otari Jam Sesh #1: Fight Night!

Two teams of local models. One messy spreadsheet. One gateway.

The Developers Wilding series continues with something smaller and faster. Jam Sesh is a one-week online mini hackathon, and this is the first one. It opens November 25th at 12:00 PM ET and closes December 2nd at 11:59 PM ET.

## Prize

Grand prize: $100. One winner.

# What do we do at this jam?

Beat the stock team.

You get a starter kit that runs Otari on your own machine, in front of a small team of local Ollama models. The kit generates a deliberately terrible CSV and has two teams clean it: the stock team, and yours. You get a fight card showing how your team did against the stock team on the same file, on the same hardware.

Your team is one file, team.yml. You don't write code. You pick the models, the batch sizes, the prompts, and how the job gets split between stages. Then you make it win.

Everything runs locally.

Bring your coding agent. The repo has an AGENTS.md that tells it what it can edit and what gets you disqualified. The fight is still local. Every model call goes through Otari on your machine and the card shows it.

# What is Otari?

Otari by Mozilla AI is an open-source AI infrastructure platform that lets you build applications and agents with the models you choose, including open-weight models.

For this jam, you run Otari yourself as the gateway every model call goes through. The starter kit starts it for you with Docker. The dashboard shows every request, and your fight card is built from Otari's own usage data.

# How do I sign up and participate?

1. Sign up through DoraHacks with this info:

- Your name or pseudonym
- One sentence on your machine (RAM and GPU)

2. Please star the Otari repo on GitHub: [https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari](https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari)
3. Open the starter kit and click "Use this template" to make your own public copy: //[https://www.github.com/mozilla-ai/otari-fight-night ](https://)
4. Install what the kit needs: Ollama, Docker, uv and make. The README has the details.
5. Run `make fight`. The first run pulls the model (about 2 GB) and takes a few minutes. `ROWS=20 make fight` is the quick version.
6. Edit team.yml and the prompts, run it again, keep going until you beat the stock team. Every fight gets saved under runs/, and `uv run fight.py compare` shows what changed between two of them.
7. Questions? Join the Mozilla OSAI Discord: [https://discord.gg/TqvzGH9mwz](https://discord.gg/TqvzGH9mwz)

# Rules

To be eligible for the prize:

- Local models only. Your fight card must show "Requests served locally: 100%". Jam Sesh #2 will open things up to remote models.
- Plain public Ollama tags. No -cloud tags (the kit refuses them) and no custom Modelfiles.
- Your team must fit in 16 GB of RAM. Top entries are rerun on a 16 GB machine.
- Scored settings: PRESET=medium and ROWS=50. These are the defaults.
- Leave the stock team and the referee alone. We check your card's Integrity section against the repo's history before we rerun anything.
- Reading the generator is fine. Put the vendor list, the category synonyms, whatever you find in there, into your prompts. Pasting golden rows or dataset ids is not fine, and the card's answer-key check has to come back clean.
- We never publish the scoring seed. We rerun the top entries on it ourselves, and that result is the one that counts. Your card gets you into the top five. The rerun picks the winner.

# Judging rubric

Scored out of 100 points.

| Criterion | Points | What judges look for |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Beat the stock team | 30 | Your net-repair score minus the stock team's, on your machine. It has to hold up when we rerun your team on the scoring seed. |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Architecture story | 25 | Why you split the job this way. A stage only counts if the log shows it changed the result. |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Pound for pound | 20 | Net repair per GB of model weights, and seconds taken. Small and fast beats big and slow. |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Show and tell | 15 | A video of up to 3 minutes that shows the fight and explains what you changed. |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Friction log | 10 | Specific, honest answers to the three feedback questions. |
| --- | --- | --- |

# Submission requirements

DEADLINE: December 2nd, 11:59 PM ET

- Link to your public GitHub repo, made from the starter kit template. It must include:
    - Your team.yml and every prompt it uses
    - SUBMISSION.md filled in, with your fight-card.md pasted into it
- Link to a demo video, up to 3 minutes. Show `make fight` running, your fight card, and what you changed in team.yml and why.
    - The video cannot use AI. It must be a screen recording with audio of you demonstrating your team. If you need an accommodation for accessibility reasons, message Marcus before you submit.
- Written feedback. Please answer these three questions:
    - Where did setup or the fight slow you down or break? Share steps to reproduce if you can.
    - What did you look for in Otari (dashboard, logs, config) and not find?
    - Would you put Otari in front of your own local models after this? Why or why not?
- An email address we can reach you at if you win.

If your submission does not include these items, you will not be eligible for the prize.

# Winner

The winner is announced on the Mozilla OSAI livestream on December 8th, where we run the winning team live.

–

If you have any questions, join the Discord (https://discord.gg/TqvzGH9mwz) and tag @Marcus. I'll respond as I'm able.

Take care!
